items.title: Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-10-21
items.q: You see, the way he played that Westlund, he had such an expression in the tone, and he'd hold him most to the evangelist. And he'd get off it short and smooth. I was playing, I had to stop myself.

ctx.x: Well, the number that gets me is that Westlund, you know, that's a beautiful part.

But, oh, no, let me tell you. The Westlund, it's even but one man ever played that thing on a baritone like he should be played. Because we was the first one in the good time, in the goddamn restaurant. Celestine, the first one, got that restaurant. A fella called John, quote it, and he's Dick. Dick, of course, you talk about God, that man, when he first got this piece, that man made everyone cry around the church. You see, the way he played that Westlund, he had such an expression in the tone, and he'd hold him…
When you were saying that he had everybody in the church crying, did he play it inside the church?
